concept.title: Periodic Password Changes
concept.shortdesc: Review network passwords regularly. Change a password when it is a default password, is no longer secure, or is known by an unauthorized person.

section.title: Overview
section.p: Network passwords protect the Wi-Fi network, guest network, connected devices, and router configuration.
Review these passwords regularly. Change a password when there is a security reason or when an applicable policy requires the change.
section.note: Do not continue to use a default password. Create a long and unique password during the initial setup.

A fixed password-change schedule is not sufficient by itself. Review account access, password exposure, connected devices, and applicable security requirements before you decide whether to change a password.

section.title: Passwords to Review
section.p: Review the passwords for the following network components and services:

ul.li: The primary Wi-Fi network identified by
The guest network identified by
The for the
Access points and mesh nodes
IoT devices and their associated accounts
Network storage devices, printers, cameras, and other managed devices

section.note: Use a different password for each account or network function. Do not use the as the password for the .

section.title: When to Change a Password
section.p: Change a network password in any of the following conditions:

ul.li: The password is a default password.
The password is weak or easy to guess.
An unauthorized person knows or can access the password.
An unknown device has connected to the network.
The password appears in an unprotected document, message, or shared file.
A person who knew the password no longer requires access.
A network device is lost, stolen, transferred, or disposed of.
A security event or device compromise can have exposed the password.
An applicable security policy requires a password change.

section.note: Change an exposed password immediately. Do not wait for the next scheduled password review.

section.title: Effects of a Password Change
section.p: Changing a Wi-Fi password disconnects devices that use the previous password.
After a password change, enter the new password on each authorized device. Remove or block devices that must no longer connect to the network.
Changing the administrator password ends the current management session on some devices. Sign in to the with the new password after the change.
section.note: Make a list of authorized devices before you change the Wi-Fi password. Update each device after you apply the new password.
Plan the password change to reduce service interruption. Identify devices that use stored credentials, including access points, mesh nodes, printers, cameras, and IoT devices.

section.title: Recommended Password Change Sequence
section.p: Change and verify passwords in the following sequence:

ol.li: Create a configuration backup for the .
Sign in to the with the new administrator password.
Change the password for the primary Wi-Fi network.
Change the guest network password if required.
Review and change the credentials for IoT and other managed devices when required.
Verify local network and Internet access.

section.note: Do not change several unrelated network settings during a password change. This practice makes connection problems more difficult to identify.

section.title: Strong Password Requirements
section.p: Each new password must be long, unique, and difficult to guess.
Follow the password requirements shown in the or the applicable device management interface.
Do not include the following information in a password:

ul.li: A person's name
An address or telephone number
A date of birth
The product name or model number
The Wi-Fi network name
Repeated or sequential characters
A password used for another account

section.note: Use a trusted password manager to create and store unique passwords.
Prefer password length and uniqueness over predictable character substitutions. Use a long passphrase when the applicable device supports it.
section.p: For more information, see .

section.title: Password Storage
section.p: Store network passwords in a secure location. Limit access to authorized users.
Use a trusted password manager when one is available.
Do not store a network password in:

ul.li: An unprotected text file
An unprotected spreadsheet
An email message
A shared document
A publicly accessible location
A label that unauthorized persons can see

section.note: Do not include operational passwords in published documentation, screenshots, configuration examples, or support records.

section.title: Password Sharing
section.p: Share the primary Wi-Fi password only with authorized users.
Give visitors access to instead of .
Change the guest network password when a visitor no longer requires access or when an unauthorized person obtains the password.
section.note: Use a guest-network schedule, expiration control, or temporary credential when the supports these functions.

section.title: Verify a Password Change
section.p: After you change a network password, verify the following conditions:

ul.li: The previous password no longer permits access.
Authorized devices can connect with the new password.
Client devices can access local network resources as permitted.
Client devices can access Internet services.
The new administrator password permits access to the .
Guest devices can connect only to .
Unknown or unauthorized devices do not appear on the .

section.note: Verify the device name and MAC address before you block a device. Some devices use private or randomized MAC addresses.

section.title: Password Change Record
section.p: Keep a record of each password change.
Record the following information:

ul.li: The date and time of the change
The affected network, account, or device
The reason for the change
The person or role that approved the change
The devices that were reconnected
The verification tests that were completed
The result of each verification test

section.note: Do not record the old password or the new password in the password change record.
Use an approved change-management record when several administrators manage the network. Record the effect of the change and the recovery method without recording credential values.
